text:
jessica_cust: Hey team, our Private deployment in ACME VPC can't reach api.redwood.com since last night. Calls go through corp-proxy and we see TLS handshake failures (502/ssl). Any ideas?

maria_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the curl/openssl output? Does the proxy do TLS termination (re-encrypt) or passthrough?

jessica_cust: curl -v output (redacted):
* Connected to proxy.corp.example (10.10.8.1) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to proxy.corp.example:443
* Closing connection 0

And when we try to bypass with openssl to the proxy (to reproduce):
```
openssl s_client -connect proxy.corp.example:443 -servername api.redwood.com -tls1_2
```
output shows: "handshake failure" and later "No peer certificate available" and "Cipher is (NONE)"

maria_support: Thanks. That usually means the proxy is terminating TLS and then re-establishing upstream TLS with a cipher/protocol that the Redwood edge refuses. Can you run s_client directly to the Redwood edge from a host that replicates the proxy outbound (if possible):
```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example.net:443 -servername api.redwood.com -tls1_3
```
If that succeeds, then the proxy is the likely culprit (rewriting SNI or using a forced cipher list). Also include the proxy TLS profile (cipher suites / TLS versions).

jessica_cust: I don't have direct egress from that subnet. But we do have the proxy TLS profile: policy forces RSA key-exchange suites and has ECDHE disabled for re-encrypt. TLS versions allowed: TLS1.0-TLS1.2 (TLS1.3 disabled)

leo_sre: That combination can break modern endpoints. Our load balancer has been hardened: we disabled RSA key-exchange ciphers (we require ECDHE and AEAD) and TLS1.3 only for some frontdoors internally. If the proxy re-encrypts with RSA-only suites or downgrades SNI, the handshake will fail.

maria_support: Two quick repro checks / mitigations you can try: 
1) Ask the proxy team to enable ECDHE suites for re-encrypt or allow TLS passthrough for *.redwood.com. Passthrough avoids header/SNI rewrite and preserves the original TLS.
2) As a temporary client-side test, run curl forcing TLS1.2 and an ECDHE cipher to see if proxy will negotiate that upstream:
```
curl -v --tlsv1.2 --ciphers 'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256' https://api.redwood.com/health
```
If that succeeds, it's confirmation the proxy just wasn't offering ECDHE to upstream.

jessica_cust: Tried the curl suggestion from a host that hits the proxy: same TLS handshake failure. Looks like proxy refused the ECDHE ciphers (policy enforced).

kevin_eng: We intentionally removed RSA key-exchange ciphers on the edge to avoid static RSA KEX vectors. We can add limited exceptions but prefer not to open RSA KEX. The correct fix is to update the proxy re-encrypt profile to support modern ECDHE+AEAD suites or switch to TCP passthrough for Redwood endpoints.

leo_sre: Also check SNI. Some proxies replace SNI with corp.example so upstream sees the wrong hostname and presents a cert that doesn't match api.redwood.com, which also causes TLS failures. To check SNI you can run: 
```
openssl s_client -connect proxy.corp.example:443 -servername api.redwood.com -tls1_2 -showcerts
```
If the cert CN isn't api.redwood.com, the proxy is rewriting SNI/terminating.

maria_support: I'll escalate to engineering to confirm the server-side cipher policy and look up which loadbalancers front the customer's region. In parallel, please open a change request with your proxy team to: enable ECDHE suites for re-encrypt (TLSv1.2+), or configure passthrough for api.redwood.com endpoints, and ensure SNI is preserved.

jessica_cust: Thanks — I'll open a request and keep you posted. One question: do you publish a list of CIDRs and hostnames we can use for passthrough rules?

maria_support: Yes — for Private/VPC egress we publish the canonical hostnames and IP ranges in our docs. Quick reference (temporary): api.redwood.com (A records vary by region) — best practice: passthrough by hostname/SNI rather than individual IPs. We'll DM the full doc link and a short-lived IP list for your specific region. :thumbsup:

kevin_eng: Follow-up: if you cannot change the proxy immediately, we can temporarily open an exception on our edge to accept a small set of RSA KEX suites for your customer tenant only while you transition the proxy — but that'll require an internal security exception and a ticket. Maria, can we track that?

maria_support: Got it, filing internal security exception request and tagging eng-sre + security. @kevin_eng please include the exact cipher strings you can allow.

deploy-bot: Ticket CREATED: SEC-9142 — temporary RSA-KEX exception request for acme-corp private deployment. Assignee: kevin_eng. SLA: 72h.

jessica_cust: Appreciated. Will coordinate with proxy team to flip to ECDHE ASAP and report back.

maria_support: Thanks — keep this thread updated. If you can provide proxy TLS profile and a pcap of the handshake (no payloads) that would speed root-cause analysis.

jessica_cust: Will do, uploading the pcap to the ticket.

maria_support: Closing loop: likely root cause = proxy TLS termination + RSA-only re-encrypt + SNI rewrite. Fix paths = enable ECDHE+AEAD on proxy re-encrypt or enable passthrough, or temporary edge exception.

jessica_cust: ✅
